 They’re also repairing dangerously uneven part of sidewalk in Montclair district

 The city of Oakland is fixing a section of root-compromised sidewalk that has presented a hazard for pedestrians behind a Montclair district Safeway for several years. (Ginny Prior for Bay Area News Group) 
 By Ginny Prior | Columnist PUBLISHED: November 3, 2026 at 5:30 AM PST | UPDATED: November 3, 2026 at 5:33 AM PST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Autumn is ushering in changes in the Oakland hills. Not only are Oakland Public Works crews cleaning storm drains and preparing for a super El Nino, but they’ve also been working this week to fix a section of dangerously uneven sidewalk behind a Montclair district Safeway. The walkway has been compromised for years by tree roots that have pushed up sections of concrete.

 Eye on the Hills: Flower mural blooms in Oakland’s Montclair district 
 Meanwhile, construction began this week on the former Rite Aid store on Mountain Boulevard in Montclair. The project manager says the space will basically be gutted and remodeled to make way for a CVS drug store to move in from their location across the street. The new location will give CVS an estimated 25,000 square feet, about four times the space of the store in which they’ve been operating.
 Food news: The new “soft” opening date for Asian/American restaurant Piggie’s is anticipated this week for Thursday as owners work through city inspection delays.
 The mother/daughter team behind the Montclair Village restaurant has designed a warm and lively space in the former site of Pagarung Thai at 6200 Antioch St. One notable change — a bar area where customers can drink and dine, not unlike Daughter Thai, where Piggie’s co-owner Alex Piyapanee worked for 11 years.
 On the other end of Montclair, the wildly successful Yellow Door is making progress on a major remodeling project. The coffee shop and café is expanding into the space that was last occupied by The Fifth Quarter Charcuterie — which will more than double Yellow Door’s square footage. The restaurant’s owners, Beth Barrett and Virginia Davis, have seen lines out their door since they opened in 2020.
 Chef collaborations: The Claremont Resort & Club near the Oakland-Berkeley border is pairing up with Hotel Valley Ho in Scottsdale, Arizona (near Phoenix), for two chef-driven dinners this fall.
 Executive Chefs Joseph Paire (Claremont) and Executive Chef Russell LaCasce (Hotel Valley Ho) are putting on a five-course dinner at Limewood Bar & Restaurant this week, with a cocktail reception followed by the multicourse showcase of dishes from both chefs. The second dinner is set for Nov. 12 in Scottsdale. Both hotels are historic, and the idea is to celebrate promote travel between the Bay Area and Phoenix.
 Another celebrated chef collaboration is coming Nov. 12-13 to the Montclair Thai restaurant Payakk (5761 Thornhill Drive). Bangkok’s Michelin-starred chef Duangporn “Bo” Songvisava, is making her first U.S. visit to partner with Payakk chef Nattaporn Pinpech, who goes by Chef Tobb.
 The dinner will explore the intersection of traditional Thai medicine, modern nutritional science and Thailand’s rich culinary heritage, taking guests on a journey through nine flavors and four elements — earth, wind, fire and water. The menu will highlight local, seasonal, whole-food ingredients and traditional Thai cooking techniques.
 Vendor opportunities: The Montclair Village Association is accepting applications from vendors who want to sell their merchandise at this year’s Holiday Stroll from 4 to 8 p.m. Dec. 10. The stroll is a major event in Montclair, with live music, caroling, holiday shopping, craft beverages and photos with Santa.
 It also caters to kids with a family zone and a story time in the former Great Good Place for Books store sponsored by the Oakland Public Library’s Montclair branch. For adults, there will be a hospitality hut with a full bar serving “festive libations” with proceeds going to the business district. The details are at montclairvillage.com .
